clue.text: Decree: no one to provide weapons

indicators.note: 'no one' asks for the numeral one to be absent, so that letter is dropped from the decree word

parts.note: an ordinance is a decree or official order
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A ruler's edict announces that nobody will be supplied with arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military supplies, especially artillery and guns, so it stands for weapons collectively.

clue.text: Drunk on account of having to drink gin neat?

definitions.meaning: slang for intoxicated, insensible with drink

definitions.text: on account of having to drink gin neat?
definitions.meaning: 'out of' means because of, and gin taken neat is gin with the It (Italian vermouth, as in 'gin and It') run out

explanation.surface: Someone excuses their drunkenness by having had to take their gin straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin and It' is a classic British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth; with no It left, you are reduced to neat gin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means intoxicated or not fully aware, a casual synonym for drunk.

clue.text: Incomplete ending of tension around border brings harm

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the border word, holding it inside
something incomplete lacks its final part, so the last letter of the word for easing tension goes

parts.note: detente is an easing or ending of tension between nations
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A partial thaw between rivals, ringed by frontier disputes, causes damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' trims the last letter, leaving DETENT, and 'around' wraps that round the border word; 'tension' tempts as the definition but harm is the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is loss or damage, a direct synonym for harm.

clue.text: A learner, boy you will interrupt and put down

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so the word for you breaks into the boy

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A learner driver and a boy are cut short by you and squashed.
explanation.definitionFit: To allay is to quell or calm fears, so allayed means put down in the sense of suppressed.

clue.text: Outcry about what the romantic French indulge in

parts.words: what the romantic French indulge in

explanation.surface: A protest erupts over what amorous French people are fond of.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud public demand or protest, much like an outcry.

clue.text: Coarse cloth useless to the Spanish

parts.note: duff is British slang for useless or broken

explanation.surface: Rough fabric is no good to people in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Duffel is a thick woollen fabric with a heavy nap, used for coats and bags.

clue.text: Duke is taking time to imprison number in disgrace

indicators.note: the time word imprisons the number word, holding it inside

parts.note: an hour is a measure of time

explanation.surface: A nobleman is jailed for a spell and his number is up in shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonour is loss of honour or reputation, the same as disgrace.

clue.text: Feeling of apprehension about the thing of little importance

indicators.note: the fear word goes about, around, the word the

parts.note: fear is a feeling of apprehension

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a trivial matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather is proverbially weightless, so it serves as a figure for something trifling.

clue.text: Record old name for gut

parts.note: to enter data is to record it

explanation.surface: Log the antiquated term for the intestines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old name' looks like one phrase meaning an archaic term, but it splits into O and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The enteron is the alimentary canal, a technical word for the gut.

clue.text: It's a little odd, what suggestive material does

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters I, T and S

explanation.surface: A remark that something is slightly peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy material excites or arouses, which is what titillating means.

clue.text: Pretentiously cultural, but not at first social

indicators.note: the opening letter is not there, so the first letter of the social word is dropped

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering

explanation.surface: A gathering is described as affectedly highbrow, though not initially.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone making a show of artistic or cultural interests, pretentiously so.

clue.text: Sweet lady or hag with deformity in disguise?

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kindly woman appears as a misshapen crone, perhaps in a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: In fairy tales the kindly helper often appears first as an ugly old woman, so the surface suits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy godmother of pantomime is a benevolent, sweet female figure who grants wishes.

clue.text: Plodder needs time with university lecturer

parts.note: a reader is a senior lecturer at a British university

explanation.surface: A slowcoach needs extra time with their tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a reader ranks just below a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A treader walks or tramps steadily, so it can describe a plodder.

clue.text: Bewitched fellows sang to put maiden off

indicators.note: 'put maiden off' says to remove the maiden letter, the first part of the signal
completes 'put off', telling us to take the maiden letter away

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Enchanted men sang to discourage a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... off' removes M from MEN CHANTED; M for maiden is a cricket scorecard convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchanted means under a spell, the same as bewitched.

clue.text: Driving until temperature falls, then stopping

indicators.note: the temperature letter falls away, dropping out of the driving word

explanation.surface: A motorist keeps going until it gets colder, then pulls up.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring is securing a boat at a berth, bringing it to a stop.

clue.text: One dive taking money in Thailand once as B and B

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a dive is a seedy bar, a den

explanation.surface: A guest saves money at a seedy Thai guesthouse, a bed and breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B and B' is not bed and breakfast but two identical letters B.
explanation.definitionFit: Two letters B are exactly alike, which is what identical means.

clue.text: Take away last of harvest to get transported back

the final letter of the harvest word is taken

explanation.surface: Remove the final crop to have it carried back.
explanation.walkthrough: T plus CARTED gives TCARTED, and 'back' reverses it all.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract from something is to take away from its value.

clue.text: It's no longer enough to be a model

explanation.definitionFit: An example is a model or pattern to follow.

clue.text: I greet a stranger in town

explanation.surface: I welcome an unfamiliar person in the town.

explanation.definitionFit: Reigate is an English town, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Affirm what a top female academic wouldn't want to be called

explanation.definitionFit: To profess is to declare or affirm openly.

clue.text: Colourful substance FBI agents found in den

explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives colour.

clue.text: The city in America has gold and the country nothing

explanation.surface: An American city is rich while the nation is broke.
